english: 128. The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
There is none.
After these things, Mahdi set out for the land of the Romans,
and encamped on the river Pyramos in the region of Arabissus.
His son Harun captured the fortress of Semalouos {OCR?}, took captives, and withdrew.
And in the year 1092,
of the Greeks, the Arabs took about seven thousand captives from Ephesus;
and four thousand of the Arabs also died.
But Emperor Leo sent an army, and they deported the orthodox Syrian population
and settled them in Thrace.
And it is said
that this Emperor Leo too hated images and persecuted the orthodox, like his father.
In that same year Leo died,
and his son Constantine reigned for twenty-two years.
Because he was young when he became emperor,
his mother Irene governed and was proclaimed ruler along with him.
In the year 1094,
1094, Mahdi sent his son Harun against the imperial city.
The Romans devised a stratagem
and hemmed in the Arabs on the river Sangarius,
with a mountain on one side
and water on the other.
When the Arabs found themselves hard pressed,
they sought peace for three years.
And Irene, reasoning like a woman, agreed,
and the Arabs withdrew.
After a year, Ali built Hadath.
After Mahdi, his son Musa reigned for one year and a month and a half.
Before this man became ruler,
namely, in the year 1095,
1095 {OCR?} of the Greeks (784 of our Lord),
flying locusts came and destroyed the crops,
and laid eggs.
They hatched and swarmed, climbing up walls and foundations,
and entering houses through windows and doors.
Even the water skins, beds, tables, and jars were filled with them.
And as they entered a house from the south,
they came out on the north side {OCR?}.
Along with the grass and trees, they also devoured woollen articles and people's clothes.
When they had devastated the whole region of Edessa and Serugh,
they passed on westward.
And for three years after this harsh chastisement,
there was famine in the land.
And in the year 1097,
1097, the Romans marched out and ravaged Hadath, which had recently been built by the Arabs;
they laid it waste and demolished its walls completely.
In that same year Musa died in the month of July.
After Musa, his brother Harun al-Rashid reigned for twenty-three years and two months.
He sent Abd al-Malik,
and he demolished the church
